title: Police lawyer questions inquest finding ; All signs point to suicide, he argues: [Ontario Edition]
article: A lawyer who represented two police officers involved in the shooting death of a Bradford man says jurors in the inquest should have come back with a finding of "suicide."

The jury looking into the death of Mark Graham, 38, who was shot outside a Bradford Tim Horton's, decided yesterday the death was "undetermined." In a public inquest, the jury can only come back with findings of either suicide, homicide, or undetermined.

"I was hoping the verdict would come back as suicide," Leo Kinahan, the lawyer for the two officers, said at coroner's court in downtown Toronto after the decision. The lawyer pointed to several pieces of evidence throughout the inquest that suggested Graham- described by witnesses as being depressed- had actually lured police into shooting him on July 29, 2001.
"The fact (is) he made no attempt to elude police. He didn't try to run or hide.

"He walked down a main street and toward a Tim Horton's that he knew police could not let him enter, because he was carrying a bag that we know had at least one semi-automatic firearm in it," Kinahan pointed out, arguing this all suggested Graham was on a suicide mission.
Witnesses testified that officers had tried to stop Graham with pepper spray and a baton, but he continued walking toward the front door of the packed Holland St. Tim Horton's.
Graham carried a semi-automatic firearm in a bag, and had a sawed- off shotgun under his clothes.
It was only after Graham turned toward police, and started to remove the sawed-off .22-calibre rifle from underneath his shirt, that officers fired.
